clue.text: Grip without power thus becomes restrained

indicators.note: without means the letter for power is left out of the word for grip

parts.note: to clasp is to grip
P is the physics symbol for power
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: A wrestler loosening a hold that has lost its strength, so it becomes gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: Classic style is simple and elegant, free of ornament, hence restrained in its taste.

clue.text: Jazz fan closing bleak club

indicators.note: closing means the word for jazz fan shuts around the other letters

parts.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
bare means bleak, stark

explanation.surface: A jazz lover shutting down a gloomy nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub offering live entertainment such as singing and comedy.

clue.text: Film no actor could get produced?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer's first word is an anagram signal acting on its second word, and that rearrangement gives the letters of no actor; could get produced asks what produces them

explanation.surface: A film made without any actors, perhaps because none could be found.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface also works: a cartoon needs no actors on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: An animated cartoon is a film made from a sequence of drawings rather than live footage.

clue.text: Spin southern fish

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for southern
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A spin doctor talking up a fish from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Side is the British billiards and snooker word for spin put on a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, side is the sideways spin a player imparts to the cue ball by striking it off centre.

clue.text: Is youth able to become a mess?

parts.note: can means is able to
a teen is a youth, a teenager

explanation.surface: Asking whether a young person is capable of turning into a slob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is youth able' is a question, which in plain English is 'Can teen?'; mess is the military dining hall, not untidiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a dining room in a barracks or workplace, which in the forces is called a mess.

clue.text: Excellent, taken for a ride so calmed down

parts.note: def is slang for excellent, cool
someone taken for a ride has been exploited, or used

explanation.surface: A great trip on a ride at the fair leaves someone soothed and settled.
explanation.definitionFit: To defuse a tense situation is to make it less dangerous, so a defused row has been calmed.

clue.text: Release distinctive doctrine in shortened treatise

indicators.note: in means the word for doctrine goes inside the shortened treatise

parts.note: diss is a short form of dissertation, a treatise
an ism is a distinctive doctrine or theory

explanation.surface: Publishing a novel creed inside an abridged academic paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone is to let them go, whether from a job or a room, which is to release them.

clue.text: Loud and outstanding clock

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud
ace is slang for outstanding

explanation.surface: Praise for a clock that chimes loudly and keeps excellent time.
explanation.walkthrough: Clock is not the timepiece here but British slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock is British slang for the face, as in a punch in the clock.

clue.text: Perhaps late-night post exceptional bouncer worked, VIP cedes, "really staying current"

indicators.note: worked means these letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current, which stays among the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A tangled tale of a nightclub bouncer, a VIP giving way, and someone staying up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: There is a second wordplay: exceptional gives SPECIAL and a bouncer is a short-pitched delivery in cricket, giving DELIVERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Special delivery is a guaranteed fast postal service, such as one promising arrival by a set time.

clue.text: Possibly jolly tryst, we hear, run down

indicators.note: we hear means the word for tryst is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a date is a romantic tryst
to rip into someone is to run them down, criticise them harshly

explanation.surface: A romantic meeting that turns out a happy, rather run-down affair.
explanation.walkthrough: A jolly is British slang for an outing or pleasure trip, often one taken at someone else's expense.
explanation.definitionFit: A day trip is an outing there and back in a day, an example of a jolly or jaunt.

clue.text: High-street saver establishing companionship?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mutual savings institution with branches on the high street
second meaning, read literally: building up a society, a fellowship of people

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into its two plain words: building means establishing and society means companionship; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A British building society is a member-owned lender where people keep savings and take out mortgages, much like an American savings and loan.

clue.text: Study concerning the traditional CE

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
AD, Anno Domini, is the traditional label for the years now often marked CE, Common Era

explanation.surface: A student researching church history and the old way of dating years.
explanation.walkthrough: CE looks like Church of England here, but it is the Common Era, whose older name is AD.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject at university is to study it, as in reading law.

clue.text: Run literally goes round, for example, square

indicators.note: goes round means the abbreviation for literally surrounds the one for for example

explanation.surface: An instruction to a runner to do a lap of the square, taken word for word.
explanation.walkthrough: Run is a second, informal definition: split in two, the answer becomes leg it, slang for run away.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is slang for legitimate, and square means honest and above board.

clue.text: Draw river bank

parts.note: a draw in a match is a tie
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A painter sketching the bank of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of seats or keys is a row, and a tier is one row in such a stepped arrangement.

clue.text: Son burst into Grease song

indicators.note: burst into means the letter for son goes inside the word for grease

parts.note: to grease or palm someone is to bribe them
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy breaking into a number from the musical Grease.
explanation.walkthrough: Grease looks like the musical; it is the verb as in greasing someone's palm.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one from the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Passage in large part of church

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the apse is the rounded end section of a church

explanation.surface: A corridor in a big section of a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse of time is an interval or passage of time between events.

clue.text: Rat's final intention?

indicators.note: final means only the last letter of the word rat is used

parts.note: the animal's name gives the word rat, whose last letter is taken
a reason is the purpose or intention behind an act

explanation.surface: Asking what a turncoat is ultimately aiming at.
explanation.walkthrough: A rat is slang for a traitor, so the whole clue also describes what such a person finally intends.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, the crime a political rat is set on committing.

clue.text: Demand in steep dish of oysters

indicators.note: in means the word for demand sits inside the word for steep

parts.note: to sop is to soak or steep
a call is a demand, as in a call for action

explanation.surface: Insisting on a steeply priced plate of oysters.
explanation.walkthrough: Steep looks like expensive, but here it is a verb, to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is also a shallow scallop-shaped dish in which seafood such as oysters is baked and served.

clue.text: Civil char grabbing most of break on the way back

indicators.note: grabbing means the word for char holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to sear is to char or scorch

indicators.note: on the way back means the shortened word is read from right to left
most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a lucky break is a piece of luck

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady, a char, snatching part of her break on the trip home.
explanation.walkthrough: Char looks like a cleaning lady but is the verb to scorch, and break is a stroke of luck, as in a lucky break.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil and secular both describe what belongs to the state or ordinary life rather than the church, as in a civil wedding.

clue.text: Quarry in coastal feature also

indicators.note: in means the word for also sits inside the coastal feature

parts.note: a spit is a narrow point of land running out into the sea
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A quarry located on the coast as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand pit is a place where sand is dug out, a kind of quarry.

clue.text: Mouth opening from this in ready repartee

indicators.note: in means the mouth and the opening letter go inside the word for ready

parts.note: ripe means ready, as in ripe for action
os is the anatomical Latin word for a mouth or opening

indicators.note: opening from means only the first letter of this is taken

explanation.surface: A quick verbal comeback leaving someone's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp reply, the kind of retort that repartee is made of.

clue.text: Brass put aside? Clear saving succeeded with mine

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe inside, so the word for clear holds the letter for succeeded

parts.note: to net is to clear as profit
s. abbreviates succeeded in family trees
egg is old military slang for a mine or bomb

explanation.surface: An investor saving money and adding mining shares to the savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum of money saved for the future, and brass is slang for cash.

clue.text: Unsettled, I can do travels round motorway

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the motorway letter
travels means the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: M marks a British motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Someone without a fixed home boasting they can drive around the motorway network.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people move from place to place with no permanent home, so their life is unsettled.

clue.text: Chutzpah by Spain aboard vessel

parts.note: gall is impudent nerve, chutzpah
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
on means aboard, as in on the ship

explanation.surface: A cheeky stowaway sailing with Spain on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, used especially by Spain.

clue.text: Rule that limits naturism?

parts.note: the limits of naturism are its outer letters, and a single limit is one or the other

explanation.surface: A nudist club regulation restricting how far members may go.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split up reads 'N or M', a way of naming one limit (end letter) of naturism.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a standard or accepted rule of behaviour, the pattern people are expected to follow.

clue.text: Latest info force ignored in volatile matter identifying scum

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the latest betting information on a horse, hence the latest info

indicators.note: ignored in means the letter for force is left out of the word that follows

parts.note: fume is vapour, a volatile substance
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A scientist analysing the latest data on vapour to identify a contaminant.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is short for starting price, the final odds on a horse and so the latest information; in Britain 'what's the SP?' means 'what's the news?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spume is froth or foam, the scum that gathers on the surface of liquid or waves.

clue.text: Heading to pharmacy I will get this?

definitions.text: Heading to pharmacy I will get this?

indicators.note: heading to means only the first letter of pharmacy is used

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: Someone on the way to the chemist predicting what they will come away with.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is a tablet of medicine, the thing a pharmacist hands over.

clue.text: Cheapskate farcically holds back cheese

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in the opposite direction
holds means the answer is held within the two words together

explanation.surface: A miser comically hoarding cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white, crumbly brined Greek cheese made from sheep or goat milk.

clue.text: Informally however, Queen is a divine being

parts.note: tho is the informal spelling of though, meaning however
R, Regina, is the Latin abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A casual remark that the monarch is a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse god of thunder, so he is a divine being.

clue.text: It may be sliced, examined and analysed by a superior thing?

parts.note: data that has been examined and analysed has been processed
the cheese, as in big cheese, is the top or most important thing

explanation.surface: A report that has been scrutinised and analysed by a senior figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Processed cheese is factory-made cheese that is often sold pre-cut into thin wrapped slices.

clue.text: Maritime duty is not overturned by new generation

indicators.note: overturned means the word not is turned round, as on its back

parts.note: an age is a generation, a period of time

explanation.surface: A customs rule for shipping that the next generation is not allowed to overturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage was historically a tax levied on cargo or ships according to their tonnage, a shipping duty.

clue.text: Continue scam about plague hospital's wiped out

indicators.note: about means the word for scam goes around the other letters

parts.note: a con is a scam or swindle

indicators.note: wiped out means the letter for hospital is removed

parts.note: to harry is to harass or plague
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A fraud involving an epidemic in which a hospital was destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is a phrasal verb meaning to keep going, to proceed without stopping.
